abstract: In this paper, we investigate a family of trace codes over finite fields of odd characteristic defined by two quadratic trace conditions. By analyzing the quadratic forms associated with these trace conditions and evaluating the corresponding character sums, we obtain the parameters and complete weight distributions of the codes. We further exploit the natural multiplicative orbit structure of the defining sets to obtain punctured codes and determine their parameters, weight distributions and dual distances. Moreover, we establish self?orthogonality criteria and investigate divisibility and projectivity of the constructed codes. These results give a unified treatment for arbitrary odd prime fields and for extension degrees of both parities.

title: The monotone part of Chatterjee's rank correlation
abstract: Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ measures how strongly a random variable $Y$ depends functionally on a random variable $X$, but it does not distinguish increasing, decreasing and non-monotone relationships. We ask how much of the dependence measured by $ξ$ is explained by an increasing relationship. For continuous marginals, $ξ$ is, up to a factor, a squared distance from independence in a Hilbert space geometry derived from the Sobolev scalar product for copulas. We answer it by the metric projection onto the closed convex set of stochastically increasing copulas in this geometry. The projection is explicit: it replaces every vertical section by its least concave majorant, and it coincides with the smallest stochastically increasing copula dominating the given one. It splits $ξ$ orthogonally into a monotone part $ξ^{\uparrow}$ and the squared distance to the class of stochastically increasing copulas; dually, $ξ^{\uparrow}$ is, up to a factor, the squared distance to the polar cone, which corresponds to negative quadrant dependence. The monotone part vanishes exactly for negatively quadrant dependent copulas, equals $ξ$ exactly for stochastically increasing copulas, and equals one only for the comonotonicity copula. In contrast to $ξ$, it is increasing in the concordance order and continuous with respect to weak convergence. Symmetrisation decomposes the measure of mutual complete dependence in the same way. Finally, the construction extends to arbitrary distributions via isotonic regression of conditional distribution functions. In particular, the plug-in estimator based on the empirical distribution is strongly consistent for every copula, without smoothing or tuning parameters.

title: Measurement-dependent reduction of open dynamics in the quantum phase estimation algorithm: the visible subspace and the damped Fejér kernel
abstract: For the quantum phase estimation (QPE) algorithm we study the minimal space of observables that is sufficient to predict the entire output distribution under open dynamics of the counting register. Building on the general Krylov theory of reduction, we compute the structure of this space explicitly for the full Fourier measurement. The outcome probabilities are determined by cyclic sums of the state matrix. If the adjoint generator is diagonal on the matrix units, the spectral classes inside the residue classes of the index difference modulo the register dimension $M$ give a constructive basis, an exact dimension formula, and attainable bounds: the dimension of the visible space lies between $M$ and $M^2-M+1$. The class includes independent qubit dephasing, and an analytically solvable reference model of Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) type yields a damped Fejér kernel; two random-unitary channels with the same Ramsey contrast show that higher harmonics are distinguishable in the QPE distribution. For approximate reduction we use a finite-time Gramian and an a posteriori residual estimate, with a quadratic error order for a reducing unperturbed subspace and a compatible initial state. Numerical calculations check the consistency of the representations and the behaviour of the error under non-Toeplitz perturbations.

title: The norm reveals projections in the positive unit sphere of an arbitrary C*-algebra
abstract: We show how a simple metric condition in terms of the C$^*$-norm of an arbitrary C$^*$-algebra $A$ can be employed to determine those norm-one positive elements which are projections. Concretely, if we write $S_{A^+}$ for the intersection of the positive cone and the unit sphere of $A$, we establish that an element $a \in S_{A^+}$ is a projection if, and only if, $$\{a\} = \left\{x\in S_{A^+}: \|x-z\| = 1 \hbox{ for all } z\in S_{A^+}\hbox{ with } \|a-z\|=1 \right\}.$$ This proves a conjecture which has been previously confirmed for von Neumann algebras and unital C$^*$-algebras. In the setting of not necessarily unital JB$^*$-algebras, the Shirshov--Cohn theorem is invoked to obtain a similar metric characterisation of projections. In the wider setting of JB$^*$-triples, we show how a metric characterisation in terms of inner ideals can be established to determine non-zero tripotents.

title: Log-Sobolev inequality for 2D $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ lattice gauge theory at all couplings
abstract: We prove that the log-Sobolev inequality holds for the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Wilson lattice Yang--Mills measure with arbitrary fixed inverse coupling $β$. The log-Sobolev constant depends on $β$ and $N$, but is uniform in the volume of the underlying lattice. The proof relies on a two-scale disintegration argument.

title: Bach-flat metrics and global regularity of conformal structures
abstract: We study global regularity properties of conformal structures on compact manifolds with applications to conformally invariant variational problems. We find sharp conditions ensuring that a manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric of Sobolev class is conformally diffeomorphic to a smooth one. In particular, we prove that $W^{2,q}$ Bach-flat four-manifolds with $q > 2$ are smooth up to conformal diffeomorphisms. We also solve the Yamabe problem for $W^{2,q}$ metrics with $q > 2$ on three-manifolds under a mild conformal condition.

title: A cohomology operation encoding the octahedral axiom
abstract: We introduce a new secondary cohomology operation, the naturality defect product, associated with a graded natural transformation between the cohomology functors of two differential graded functors, and study its main properties. We then prove that a pretriangulated category satisfies the octahedral axiom if and only if the naturality defect product associated with the natural isomorphism given by a theorem of Heller vanishes on the homotopy category of acyclic complexes over it. This characterization extends immediately to n-angulated categories. As an application, we exhibit non-vanishing instances for the recently found examples of pretriangulated categories which are not triangulated. Finally, we show that horizontal composition of these natural isomorphisms preserves n-angulated structures, and we use it to obtain, from each of these examples and for every r >= 1, a pre-3r-angulated category which is not 3r-angulated.

title: Regularized Sequential Reconstructions of Dynamic Nonsmooth Sources from Sparse Boundary Flux Data
abstract: We consider an inverse source problem for the heat equation on the unit disk $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with flux measurements at finitely many boundary points. The source is piecewise constant in time on prescribed intervals and, on each interval, is the characteristic function of an unknown region with Lipschitz boundary. The measurements on each interval split into the contribution of the current source and a history term from earlier sources; subtracting the latter leaves a linear inverse problem for a forward operator $F_τ$ that is densely defined and unbounded on $L^2(Ω)$. We prove that $F_τ$ is not closable, so the classical regularization theory for closed unbounded operators does not apply. We regularize instead with a Hilbert-scale penalty that compactifies it. The resulting Galerkin--Tikhonov reconstruction is sequential: each source is recovered from the flux observed up to the end of its interval and from the previously reconstructed sources. We prove its convergence and uniqueness, show that earlier reconstruction errors propagate into later data with exponential decay in time, and establish stability estimates with respect to the number of sensors. A numerical experiment on noisy measurements shows the feasibility of the sequential approximations, refined by Fourier approximation and boundary correction by a neural network.

title: Bounds on the number of squares in recurrence sequences: $y_{0}=b^{2}$ (II)
abstract: For binary recurrence sequences, $\left( y_{k} \right)_{k \in \bbZ}$, arising from the solutions of generalised Pell equations, $X^{2}-dY^{2}=c$, where $y_{0}$ is any positive square and $c=-2^{\ell}p^{m}$ for an odd prime $p$ and non-negative integers $\ell$ and $m$, we show that there are at most $4$ distinct squares with $y_{k}$ sufficiently large. From this result, we also show that there are at most $7$ distinct squares when $y_{0}=1,2^{2},\ldots,7^{2}$, or once $d$ exceeds an explicit lower bound, without any conditions on the size of such squares.

title: From Fairness to Efficiency in Repeated Bilateral Trade
abstract: Recently, Bachoc et al. (2026) proposed an axiomatic approach to fairness for repeated bilateral trade. Their resulting objective is a H\''older mean of seller and buyer utilities with non-positive order $λ$, interpolating between Rawlsian fairness at $λ= -\infty$ and Nash fairness at $λ= 0$. Here we study this family of H\''older means in the complementary setting of orders $λ\in (0,1]$, which constitutes a tradeoff between fairness and efficiency, with the weight of efficiency increasing with $λ$, and where $λ=1$ yields the existing gain from trade criterion, focusing solely on efficiency. We obtain an axiomatic characterization of these H\''older means, relying on a Pigou-Dalton principle of transferring from rich to poor. From an online learning perspective, we show that, contrary to the case $λ\le 0$, the problem is unlearnable in full generality, even under seller's and buyer's valuation independence. We focus on seller's and buyer's valuations with distributions having bounded densities, in which case we obtain matching lower and upper bounds on the cumulative regret, of order $\widetildeΘ(T^{2/3})$ with respect to the time horizon $T$. The upper bounds rely on a reconstruction identity where the expected objective is written as a gain-from-trade term plus a two-dimensional integral involving the seller and buyer distribution and survival functions, and a kernel function. For $0 < λ< 1/2$, the strong singularity of the kernel is addressed by two main ingredients. First, we propose a new zooming algorithm that sequentially rejects or refines layers of the set of prices. Second, we propose a tailored decomposition of the two-dimensional integral, enabling us to truncate it with a controlled impact on the truncation error. For $1/2 \le λ\le 1$, the singularity of the kernel is mild enough, so that the existing scouting bandit algorithm, already proposed for the case $λ=1$, can be extended.

title: Universal polynomials for Gromov-Witten invariants on toric surfaces
abstract: We study the polynomiality of combined logarithmic and ordinary Gromov-Witten invariants with a Lambda class insertion on toric surfaces $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$. We show that the combined logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants can be expressed in terms of universal relative node polynomials when the direction vector $\mathbf{c}$ and length vector $\mathbf{d}$ of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ are sufficiently large and spread out. In particular, when the normal fan of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ is smooth and its edges satisfy a length condition, we show that the combined Gromov-Witten invariants are equal to a universal node polynomial. We also show that the higher genus Block-Göttsche polynomials of smooth toric surfaces corresponding to these $h$-transverse lattice polygons, including toric blowups beyond Hirzebruch and toric del Pezzo surfaces, are equal to a generating function of higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants.

title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
abstract: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.

title: Two families of Young tableaux with periodic walls: Counting formulas and differential transcendence
abstract: Banderier, Marchal, and Wallner studied the enumeration problem for Young tableaux with walls. These are similar to standard Young tableaux, except that local decreases are allowed at some walls. In 2021, Banderier and Wallner counted Young tableaux with periodic walls, in which the elementary blocks are Young diagrams of shape $(2,2)$. They obtained exact counting formulas for $30$ of the $32$ classes up to symmetry. In this paper, we first derive recurrences for counting the remaining two classes of Young tableaux with periodic walls. We then prove that their counting exponential generating functions are differentially transcendental. Consequently, they are neither D-algebraic nor D-finite. This disproves a conjecture of Banderier and Wallner.

title: Type-II Singularities of Immersed Locally Convex Curves Evolving under Generalized Anisotropic Gage Area-Preserving Flows with Slow Curvature Speeds
abstract: In this paper, we study the singularity behavior of immersed locally convex closed plane curves evolving under generalized anisotropic Gage area-preserving flows with slow curvature speeds of the form $κ_σ^α$, where $0<α\le 1$. Here $κ_σ$ denotes the anisotropic curvature associated with a prescribed anisotropy function $σ$. We prove that every finite-time blow-up is of Type-II provided that the Euclidean length of the evolving curve remains uniformly bounded away from zero. This result holds without any symmetry assumptions on either the initial curve or the anisotropy. When the initial signed area is nonzero, this length lower bound is automatically satisfied, and thus any finite-time singularity is necessarily of Type-II. By means of Hamilton's rescaling method combined with a differential Harnack estimate, we show that along a suitable blow-up subsequence, the rescaled curves at the selected times converge locally to the profile of a translating solution of the corresponding anisotropic curvature flow $V=κ_σ^α$. We also establish sufficient conditions for finite-time singularity formation in terms of the initial signed area and anisotropic length. Moreover, we construct locally convex initial curves arbitrarily close to the Wulff curve for which a finite-time Type-II singularity occurs.

title: A Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs
abstract: Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type conditions are degree conditions for the existence of hamiltonian cycles in digraphs, which impose degree restrictions on nonadjacent vertices which have a common in-neighbor or a common out-neighbor. They can be viewed as directed analogues of both Fan-type conditions and heavy subgraph conditions in undirected graphs, and they also generalized the classes of locally semicomplete digrahs, loclaly in-semicomplete digraphs, and locally out-semicomplete digraphs. In this paper, we prove what is, to our knowledge, the first Bang-Jensen-Gutin-Li type condition for pancyclicity in digraphs. More precisely, let $D$ be a strong digraph with order $n\ge 3$. We show that, if for every $u\in V(D)$ belonging to a dominated nonadjacent pair or a dominating nonadjacent pair, we have $d(u)\ge n$, then $D$ is pancyclic, unless $D$ belongs to one of two well-characterized classes of exceptional digraphs.

title: Supercritical Geometric Optics for multidimensional scalar conservation laws
abstract: This article studies the propagation, near a smooth non-constant ground state, of monophase oscillatory wave trains with small amplitude and very high frequency for multidimensional nonlinear scalar conservation laws. These oscillations lie beyond the classical regime of uniformly bounded variation. Two scenarios may occur. Under suitable compatibility conditions, the oscillations propagate. Otherwise, they are damped through shock formation. In the baseline supercritical regime, we give an explicit criterion distinguishing these two behaviors and justify the corresponding asymptotic descriptions. At higher frequencies, the propagation mechanism becomes more restrictive and is governed by compatibility conditions involving a Lie algebra. Under a natural local constant-rank assumption, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of complete WKB expansions. We also prove cancellation under first-order incompatibility. Perturbing a non-constant background state limits the propagation of small scales compared with the constant-background case. Our constructions contribute to the understanding of the fractional smoothing effect conjectured by Lions, Perthame and Tadmor.

title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
abstract: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

title: Testing independence in contamination models
abstract: We consider a bivariate contamination model in which the distribution of a gold standard is known, while the mixing weight and the distribution of the contaminant component are unknown, and we test whether the two coordinates of the unknown component are independent. Classical independence tests are meaningless here, since a mixture of product distributions is not a product distribution. Following the Inversion-Best Matching principle, we invert the model for every candidate weight and compare the inverted distribution of the unknown component with the product of its marginals. The weight is estimated where they are closest in a Cramer-von Mises sense, and the scaled minimal distance is the test statistic. An exact quadratic structure makes the estimator computable without numerical optimisation and yields a transparent asymptotic theory under both hypotheses. The null distribution is calibrated by a multiplier bootstrap. Simulations and applications to gene expression data and spam filtering illustrate the method.

title: Number of equations defining the Kummer varieties of hyperelliptic curves
abstract: The Jacobian of an hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is equipped with a symmetric theta divisor $Θ$ that defines a principal polarization. The line bundle $\mathcal{O}(2Θ)$ defines an embedding of the Kummer variety $K$ inside the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$, which factorizes inside a certain orthogonal Grassmannian. We describe a minimal free resolution of $K$ inside this Grassmannian using geometric representation theory. As a consequence, we obtain a formula for the number of quartic equations defining $K$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$.

title: Mustafin degenerations of six points in the projective plane and self-duality
abstract: Mustafin varieties provide a framework for degenerating the projective plane together with marked points, governed by the combinatorics of Bruhat-Tits buildings. Such limit objects are parametrized by the boundary points of a projective compactification of the moduli space of $n$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ constructed by Schaffler-Tevelev. In this paper, we study the locus of this compactification generically parametrizing self-dual configurations, or equivalently, six points lying on a conic. We prove that this locus is a tropical compactification of the moduli space of self-dual configurations, with associated fan a refinement of the self-dual tropical Grassmannian introduced by Geiger-Hashimoto-Sturmfels-Vlad. We show that this compactification is a blow up of $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,6}$ and we classify the objects it parametrizes: degenerations of $\mathbb{P}^2$ equipped with a stable $6$-pointed rational curve that records the limiting conic.

title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.

title: The metastability phenomen for a radiative gas model
abstract: We study the time-asymptotic behaviour of solutions to a singular perturbation of the inviscid Burgers problem describing sound propagation in a radiating gas. This radiating gas model exhibits the interesting phenomenon known as metastability that has been first identified for the viscous Burgers equation. Precisely, on an initial time span, that scales linearly in the inverse of the perturbation parameter, we can quantify the L1-distance of the solution to the so-called sharp N-wave solution of the inviscid Burgers problem and to a diffusive N-wave. On a second long-time stage that scales exponentially in the inverse of the perturbation parameter, the solutions still remain close to a diffusive N-wave before finally collapsing into diffusion waves. Besides our analysis of the radiating gas model, we also provide an alternative description of metastability in the viscous Burgers model which, unlike other studies, relies on L1-estimates and does not require the passage to similarity variables.

title: Minimality of Binary Codes From Weight Layers and Graph Cut Spaces
abstract: Minimal binary linear codes play an important role in secret-sharing schemes and in the structural study of linear codes. We study the minimality of three classes of known constructions: codes from a single complete Hamming-weight layer, codes from arbitrary unions of such layers and graph cut-space codes. For the previously studied single-layer codes C, we give a complete minimality classification: C is minimal if and only if t is even. For t = 4, we determine the minimum and maximum weights, and show that the family strictly violates the binary Ashikhmin Barg sufficient condition for every k. We also calculate the minimum distance of the dual code. For arbitrary unions of complete Hamming-weight layers, we obtain an if-and-only-if classification of minimality and uniform criteria for evenness, self-orthogonality, the doubly even property and hull dimension. We further analyze the family for odd k. Finally, using the classical bond characterization of cuts, we translate minimality of graph cut space codes into a graph-theoretic condition: a nonempty simple graph has a minimal cut code precisely when it has one edge-containing component and that component is complete. We also give a graph-function realization of the known binary tetrahedron code and explicitly identify the resulting code equivalence.

title: Unique direct-sum decompositions of infinite-dimensional unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group via real CMV matrices
abstract:
Unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group arise naturally and play an important role in a wide range of areas including mathematics, physics, and engineering. CMV matrices, introduced by Cantero, Moral, and Velázquez, are five-diagonal unitary matrices that are standard tools in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. It is known that every unitary representation of the infinite dihedral group on a separable Hilbert space admits a discrete direct-sum decomposition into representations arising from the natural factorizations of real CMV matrices and copies of two exceptional one-dimensional irreducible representations.
  We prove that such a decomposition is unique up to unitary equivalence when the summands arising from real CMV matrices are grouped according to their multiplicities and the spectral measures of the corresponding matrices are mutually singular across distinct multiplicities. Furthermore, we show that the representation associated with each such real CMV matrix $C$ admits a direct integral decomposition into irreducible unitary representations with respect to the push-forward of the restriction of the spectral measure of $C$ to the closed upper half circle.
  These results make it possible to study the structure of unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group using CMV matrices and the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.

title: Encoding Time Series Dynamics with Sliding-Window Signatures for Online Forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting often relies on both past target values and exogenous variables as inputs. In many applications, however, the time series of interest are non-stationary and the relationship between target and inputs evolves over time, requiring forecasters that adapt online. Moreover, inputs affect the target not only through their current values but also through their recent joint dynamics. We address these challenges in three steps. First, to encode the series dynamics, we rely on signatures of the input paths over sliding windows. Motivated by the universality of linear functionals of signatures, we fit a regularized linear regression on these features to capture nonlinear, path-dependent effects. Second, the simplicity of the linear model allows us to update it online as new data arrives, using a Kalman filter to track dynamic effects. Third, to capture dependencies at several time scales, we combine forecasters built on different window lengths through online aggregation. For French national electricity load forecasting, our method outperforms various state-of-the-art approaches. It also remains competitive across several benchmark datasets with exogenous variables.

title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
abstract: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The first result states that, under the assumption of boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Under the same assumption, the second result asserts that if a multilinear operator is bounded on some weighted Lebesgue space, then its compactness can be extrapolated from some unweighted Lebesgue space to Banach function spaces. Our results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.

title: $RO(G)$-graded cohomology of a point is self-injective
abstract: Generalizing known results for $G=C_2$ and constant $\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-coefficients, we show the $RO(G)$-graded Bredon cohomology of a point with constant $\underline{k}$-coefficients is self-injective whenever $G$ is a finite subgroup of $SO(3)$ and $k$ is a finite field. Self-injectivity holds more generally for the $RO(G)$-graded homotopy of the Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum associated to a $k$-linear commutative Green functor $M$, whenever the spectrum $HM$ is Anderson self-dual.

title: Revisiting the Schwarz Lemma for the Pentablock: Counterexamples and Sharp Interpolation Criteria
abstract: Alshehri and Lykova (\emph{J. Geom. Anal.} \textbf{33} (2023)) formulated a Schwarz lemma for the pentablock $P$, giving a criterion for the existence of an analytic map from the unit disc $\mathbb D$ into the closed pentablock $\overline P$ that sends the origin to the origin and a prescribed point $λ_0\in\mathbb D$ to a given point $x_0\in\overline P$. We show that the sufficiency direction of their criterion is false. We identify the underlying error as the extension to the open unit disc of a Fejér--Riesz identity that is valid only on the unit circle. We establish a corrected necessary and sufficient interpolation criterion when the last two components are prescribed by a fixed rational $Γ$-inner function and resolve the special case $s_0=0$. Using the Poisson integral representation of the associated outer spectral factor, we obtain a sharp comparison between the corrected bound and the bound proposed by Alshehri and Lykova, with a precise characterization of equality. We further express the logarithmic difference between these bounds as a nonnegative Green potential, thereby quantifying the discrepancy in terms of the derivative of the first coordinate of the prescribed $Γ$-inner function. Finally, we formulate a variational problem over rational $Γ$-inner interpolants satisfying the prescribed two-point conditions. We show that the supremum of the associated outer-factor quantities determines the maximal admissible modulus of the first coordinate among pentablock-valued interpolants whose last two components belong to this class. Equivalently, this extremal problem reduces to minimizing the corresponding Green potential. We conclude by discussing the remaining problem of characterizing unrestricted Schwarz interpolation for the pentablock and its connection with the Lempert function.

title: Comparing and measuring intermediate tail dependence
abstract: The tail dependence function $Λ$ of a bivariate copula, and the tail dependence order based on it, cannot distinguish between copulas whose tail dependence coefficient vanishes; for all of them $Λ\equiv 0$. Such copulas, among them the Gaussian copulas with correlation $ρ<1$ and the lower tails of all extreme-value copulas other than the comonotonicity copula, are nevertheless ordered by the much finer information contained in their tail expansion $C(u w)\sim u^κ\ell(u)\,b(w)$, where $κ$ is the tail order, $\ell$ is slowly varying and $b$ is the tail order function of Hua and Joe. We introduce an asymptotic tail order $\preceq$ that refines the tail dependence order and show that it is lexicographic in the three quantities $κ$, $\ell$ and $b$. As a consequence, every real-valued measure that is monotone with respect to $\preceq$ is constant on all but countably many tail-order classes; meaningful measures of intermediate tail dependence must therefore be defined level-wise, and we construct such measures. Finally we determine where the fine structure resides: if the joint tail is ray-regular on the exponential scale, then $b$ is determined by the tail order and the one-sided derivatives at $ω=1/2$ of the angular dependence function of Wadsworth and Tawn; it is a (possibly broken) product of powers. If the joint tail is log-concave on the exponential scale, $b$ is squeezed between two such products.

title: A theoretically exact filtered back-propagationformula for single-time wave inversion
abstract: We consider single-time wave inversion, that is, recovering the initial pressure $f$ from the wave field $\mathcal{W}_T f = u(\cdot,T)$ at a single time $T$, where $u$ solves the wave equation with sound speed $c$ and initial data $(f,0)$. In two dimensions this is the main reconstruction step of full-field photoacoustic projection imaging, where each camera image is a two-dimensional wave field at a single time instant. An efficient direct method is back-propagation by the Fourier multiplier $2\cos(cT|ξ|)$. It yields exact inversion in odd dimensions but not in two. We give its error in closed form, with bounds, and derive an exact explicit filtered back-propagation $f = 2\mathcal{W}_T \mathcal{M}_K \mathcal{W}_T f$ in analogy to filtered backprojection for the Radon transform.

title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
abstract: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.

title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Hall-Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
abstract: In this paper we prove Liouville-type theorems for the stationary fractional Hall-magnetohydrodynamic equations in $\mathbb R^3$. Smooth solutions vanishing at infinity, with $u\in\dot H^{α/2}$ and $b\in\dot H^{β/2}$, are trivial for $1\leα\le\frac53$, $1\leβ<2$ and $α+2β\le5$, with no additional integrability assumption. The key step is to estimate the Hall boundary term through the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of $b$.

title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings
abstract: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.

title: On the symmetric Morrey problem in three dimensions
abstract: We study the relations between seven generalized notions of convexity for continuous integrands in the space of symmetric $3\times 3$ matrices. Here, symmetric quasiconvexity is defined through symmetrized gradients, and symmetric rank-one convexity through symmetrized rank-one lines. We construct a symmetric quasiconvex integrand that is not polyconvex at symmetric matrices, and an integrand that is both symmetric rank-one convex and Hessian quasiconvex but not symmetric quasiconvex. We also establish a transfer principle that converts smooth rank-one convex functions that lack Hessian quasiconvexity into symmetric rank-one convex integrands while preserving this lack of of Hessian quasiconvexity. Applying this scheme to already existing counterexamples yields the existence of symmetric rank-one convex integrands that are not Hessian quasiconvex. Together with known examples, these results determine all pairwise implications among the seven notions considered here.

title: Uniqueness and attractiveness of stationary solutions in a harvesting mean field game
abstract: Sustainable harvesting of natural resources is a central challenge both in ecology and economics. This paper explores a MFG model for harvesting in an aquatic ecosystem. Such systems have recently attracted attention from the applied mathematics community, and, due to the interplay between the competition of agents and the internal dynamics of the fish population, the analytical properties of the resulting system are very delicate to study. In the present work, we focus on stationary solutions, with a strong emphasis on their uniqueness and dynamical stability.

title: General Relativity for Mathematicians - Part I
abstract: These notes cover the first part of a course of the same title taught by Filippo Fila-Robattino and Manuel Tecchiolli at the University of Zurich in the Winter Semester of 2025. Topics include variational principles in classical mechanics, special relativity, smooth manifolds and tensor calculus, connections and curvature, geodesic motion, and the derivation of Einstein's equations from the Einstein-Hilbert action. The treatment is aimed at a mathematical audience, combining physical motivation with precise definitions, detailed proofs, and explicit calculations.

title: Global regularity for a class of degenerate/singular Monge-Ampere equations
abstract: We study the global regularity of solutions to the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for a class of Monge-Ampere equations, which become degenerate or singular on the boundary due to the zero boundary value and the distance function. The degeneracy and singularity are described by the index - the sum of the powers of the distance function and the solution. We give a complete classification of the index, and prove that the solution is globally Holder continuous, log-Lipschitz continuous, $C^{1,eta}$, $C^{2,alpha}$ and $W^{2,p}$ respectively, depending on the size of the index. We also obtain estimates related to the five regularity results. All these results are optimal.

title: The modular characters of $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$
abstract: Using computational methods, we determine the irreducible $3$- and $5$-modular characters of the symplectic group $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$ for blocks with non cyclic defect groups, with one ambiguity in the principal $3$-block.

title: Structure-preserving discretisations for the quasi-incompressible, thermal Maxwell-Stefan equations
abstract: We study a thermal Maxwell-Stefan-Navier-Stokes system modelling miscible mixtures under a quasi-incompressibility constraint. The system consists of the conservation laws for mass and momentum, and the balance law for entropy, which is preferred over the balance law for energy because it facilitates the development of two structure-preserving discretisation methods. The first method applies a semi-implicit Euler scheme in time, together with suitable finite elements in space, which guarantees generation of entropy and enforces the quasi-incompressibility constraint pointwise, but numerically dissipates total energy. The second method employs a continuous Petrov-Galerkin discretisation in time, which also generates entropy and satisfies the constraint pointwise, and in addition conserves the total energy and allows high-order time approximations. The structure-preserving properties and behaviour of both numerical methods are demonstrated by a series of numerical experiments.

title: Sharp Bounds for Graph-Codes Avoiding Complete Bipartite Differences
abstract:
Let $d_{K_{s,t}}(n)$ be the largest fraction of all graphs on $[n]$ in a family containing no two distinct members whose symmetric difference is a copy of $K_{s,t}$. We determine this maximum density for every fixed pair of positive integers $s,t$. If both part sizes are odd, it is known that the density is exactly $1/2$. Otherwise, let $2h$ be the largest even part size. We prove $$ d_{K_{s,t}}(n)=Θ_{s,t}(n^{-h}). $$ For $h>1$, this improves the general $O_{s,t}(1/n)$ upper bound obtained from Alon's two-copy gluing theorem~\cite{Alon2024}. The sharp bounds for even stars were already proved by Alon and are recovered as special cases.
  The upper bound uses the Frankl--Füredi forbidden-intersection theorem. For the lower bound, we construct binary linear codes using BCH codes. When exactly one part size is even, we assign to each edge the sum of the binary vectors assigned to its endpoints. When both part sizes are even, we identify these vectors with elements of a finite field and assign to each edge the product of its endpoint elements. In both cases, every copy of $K_{s,t}$ has a nonzero syndrome.

title: Smooth stationary water waves with multiple vortex spikes
abstract: For any prescribed positive integer $n$, we establish the existence of a family of stationary solutions to the two dimensional capillary-gravity water wave equations in finite depth, whose stream functions exhibit $n$ well-separated vertically aligned vortex spikes with alternating signs. The construction is based on a nonlinear gluing scheme for a singularly perturbed semilinear elliptic equation coupled to the Bernoulli equation on the free surface. Our results extend the single-spike construction to arbitrary finite multi-spike configurations and reveal a mechanism through which exponentially localized vortex spikes can coexist with an almost flat free surface.

title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
abstract: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $α$, let $λ_{k,α}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24λ_{k,α}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^α}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^αn+λ_{k,α}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(α+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.

title: A non-perturbative topological persistence theorem for normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds
abstract: Floer proved that, under a sufficiently small $C^0$ perturbation, a normally hyperbolic invariant manifold gives rise to a nearby invariant set whose cohomology ring contains a subring isomorphic to that of the original manifold. Using topological conditions, expressed in terms of the so-called covering relations, we generalize this theorem to a non-perturbative context. Our result does not require the existence of an invariant manifold before perturbation, nor does it require the original map to be smooth or invertible. For the proof, we develop an additional structure on the Conley index for maps on vector bundles.

title: Quantitative approximation theorem of neural operators for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
abstract: In this paper, we study neural operators for the Dirichet-to-Neumann map (DN map), which is encountered in the famous Calderón's problem. In many numerical methods used for reconstructing the unknown conductivity from the knowledge of the DN map need to evaluate the corresponding DN map at a given conductivity function, which involves solving the boundary value problem for the conductivity equation and taking the Neumann data. Such procedure is time consuming and not effective. Hence, it is a favorable strategy to construct a surrogate to replace the forward map mapping conductivity functions to corresponding DN maps. The main theme of this paper is to derive quantitative bounds on the parametric complexity of these neural operators. In particular, under suitable assumptions, their depth grows at most logarithmically with $\varepsilon^{-1}$, while the relevant spectral and projection ranks grow algebraically. It should be noted that general neural operators suffer from "the curse of parametric dimensionality". This work demonstrates the construction of neural operators for the DN map that does not suffer from such curse.

title: Autonomous Structural Discovery Of Bioprocess Dynamics And Kinetics Via LLM-Driven Agents
abstract: High-fidelity digital twins in continuous biomanufacturing are often bottlenecked by incomplete kinetic models, while standard data-driven algorithms (e.g., SINDy, PINNs) lack interpretability or impose rigid physical assumptions. This paper introduces a hybrid closed-loop architecture for autonomous kinetic state-space discovery driven by a Large Language Model (LLM) agent. The framework employs a sequential "isolation-peeling" methodology across orthogonal operational regimes. This algorithmic peeling mathematically decouples entangled multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (catalytic) biological rate law. Grounded in a Two-Level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) library, the framework utilizes Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) and logarithmic decomposition to decouple complex cell growth kinetics into orthogonal multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (regulatory) residual channels. When statistical degeneracy occurs an Active Design of Experiments (DoE) controller dynamically triggers targeted perturbations to decorrelate competing model hypotheses. Evaluated on a continuous stirred-tank reactor exhibiting unmodeled Haldane inhibition, Luong product toxicity, and secondary metabolite autocatalysis, the framework autonomously expanded the state space and recovered ground-truth parameters with under 6% error without a priori kinetic knowledge.

title: Square-Root Clustered Lasso for High-Dimensional Linear Regression with Finite-Sample Theory and Efficient Algorithm Implementation
abstract: This paper proposes a square-root clustered Lasso penalized method for high-dimensional linear regression. By integrating square-root loss with the clustered Lasso penalty, the resulting method enables flexible regression modeling and allows tuning parameter selection independent of the unknown noise level. We establish weak decomposability of the clustered Lasso penalty and a noise-level-free tuning strategy under Gaussian noise. Furthermore, we establish the finite-sample prediction accuracy guarantees for the proposed method. The inherent nonsmoothness of the square-root loss and clustered Lasso penalty poses considerable computational difficulties. To resolve this issue, we develop an efficient semismooth Newton-based proximal augmented Lagrangian algorithm (N-ALM) to solve the corresponding dual optimization problem. The subproblems arising in the iteration are efficiently tackled by the semismooth Newton method, which fully utilizes the sparsity structure of the generalized Jacobian. We further establish global convergence and a local linear rate for the distance to the KKT solution set under suitable conditions; the local rate becomes superlinear when the penalty parameter tends to infinity. We conduct numerical experiments on real-world datasets to evaluate the computational performance of N-ALM. The results demonstrate that N-ALM solves the tested high-dimensional SRCL problems accurately and substantially reduces running times compared with d-ADMM.

title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a relative BFK gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to Lück and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles.

title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a positive global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a positive local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. Our main tool is a reduction of $s$-principal compression to a rank-$k$ singular value perturbation. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
abstract: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

title: A Robust ADI-Based Direct Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Two-Dimensional Singularly Perturbed Parabolic PDEs
abstract: This study proposes two-dimensional one-parameter singularly perturbed parabolic problems and develops an operator-splitting direct discontinuous Galerkin (DDG) method for their numerical solution. To improve computational efficiency, an alternating direction implicit (ADI) splitting approach decomposes the original two-dimensional problem into two separate one-dimensional subproblems. The spatial discretization is performed using the DDG method on a piecewise-uniform Shishkin mesh, enabling accurate resolution of the sharp boundary layers that arise in singularly perturbed problems (SPPs). For the temporal discretization is carried out with the backward Euler scheme to ensure robustness and stability. The theoretical analysis establishes an optimal convergence rate of order $k$ in the spatial discretization, where $k$ denotes the degree of the polynomial basis functions, and $(Δt)$-order convergence in temporal dimensions. We prove that the resulting fully discrete scheme is consistent, stable, and convergent. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

title: Self-consistent flow maps based on commutator-free exponential integrators
abstract: We develop a flow-map framework for nonlinear transport equations, comprising a self-consistent exact frozen flow and its numerical realization. An exponential--pullback identity represents each frozen transport exponential in a commutator-free exponential integrator as the pullback induced by its exact backward characteristic map. Composing these maps defines the self-consistent exact frozen flow, a time-discrete construction with autonomous frozen fields formed from linear combinations of transport fields evaluated at the stage approximations. A local freezing-error identity and a one-step estimate for the Lie--Euler Vlasov--Poisson update separate field variation, field approximation, and characteristic integration errors; these estimates do not assert global PDE convergence. We specialize this construction to the Vlasov--Poisson system and obtain the self-consistent numerical flow through velocity-space quadrature, a discrete Poisson solve, field interpolation, and numerical integration of the frozen characteristic equations. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we prove that the self-consistent exact frozen flow for this system is a volume-preserving diffeomorphism. Temporal self-convergence tests on Vlasov--Poisson and guiding-center benchmarks yield rates consistent with the design orders and illustrate conservation behavior and the evolution of solution structures in long-time simulations with large time steps.

title: A Numerical Method for the Fractional Semilinear Calderón Problem
abstract: We present a finite element method for reconstructing a coefficient in a fractional semilinear equation from a single exterior measurement.

title: Scott-type inequalities for trinomial $h^*$-polynomials
abstract:
Motivated by Scott's inequality for lattice polygons, we study normalized volume bounds for lattice polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ with $h^*$-polynomials $1+at^k+bt^\ell$, where $a,b\ge1$ and $1\le k<\ell$. For $\ell>2k$, the coefficients satisfy $a+1\le b$, and consequently ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le2b$. In the complementary range $k<\ell\le2k$, we establish the dimension-independent bound \[
  {\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le(2b+1)(k+\ell). \] On the boundary $\ell=2k$ with $b\ge2$, the sharper Scott-type inequality ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le4k(b+1)$ holds, confirming a conjecture of Higashitani, Nill, and the author. Equality holds if and only if $k=1$ and $a=3b+3$. Moreover, when $\ell=2k$ and $k,b\ge2$, we obtain an upper bound depending only on $b$.

title: Regular Graphs Without Isomorphic Bisections
abstract: A graph is bisectable if its vertex set can be split into two sets inducing isomorphic subgraphs. Ando conjectured that every cubic graph is bisectable, and Das, Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov proved it for large enough connected cubic graphs. We give a constructive proof that, for every $d\geq5$, there exists a non-bisectable $d$-regular graph of even order.

title: Continuity of the phase transition for long-range Bernoulli percolation with exponential decay on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$
abstract: We prove continuity of the phase transition for long-range Bernoulli percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ with connection probabilities that decay at least exponentially fast. This extends earlier work by Duminil-Copin, Sidoravicius, and Tassion on slabs. Our proof establishes a finite-size criterion that allows us to run a renormalisation argument. As a corollary, we obtain supercritical sharpness, in the sense that for every $β>β_c$, there exists a unique macroscopic cluster in large boxes with high probability.

title: Large deviations for observables with logarithmic singularity and differentiability of the pressure function
abstract: We show that logarithmic observables of form $φ(x)=\log(|x-b|)$ on the doubling map $T$ have exponential large deviations with respect to the invariant measure if $b$ is preperiodic but not periodic with respect to $T$ giving a counterpart to the known result of strictly stretched exponential large deviations in the case that $b$ is periodic. These results are established by showing that the topological pressure function developed for unbounded observables is differentiable at $0$.

title: Falconer estimate for circular and cinematic Furstenberg problem
abstract: We prove the Falconer-type bound $\dim_{\mathrm H}F\geq u+1$ for planar circular $(u,v)$-Furstenberg sets whenever $0<u\leq1$, $0<v\leq3$, and $2u+v\geq3$. The same bound holds for smooth cinematic curve families. This resolves the circular Furstenberg conjecture of Green, Harris, Ou, Ren, and Tammen in its full Falconer range $2u+v\geq3$.

title: A PDE-Based Model of Runner Flow in Mass Participation Events
abstract: This paper presents a macroscopic approach for modeling pedestrian movement. A convection-diffusion partial differential equation (PDE) is described and used to model the flow of runners along a marathon course. A marathon is a good modeling case study for human movement because the location of runners is only known in sparse locations, so an accurate model is needed to know where people are at all times. As well, marathons offer many safety and logistical problems that can be solved by modeling human movement. Data is obtained from the 2023 Columbus Marathon, and model improvements are made to include a temporally varying convection term. Results show an increase in model accuracy which can allow for better resource allocation and safety measures.

title: Global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ Convergence of Multilevel Gradient-Regularized Newton Methods
abstract: We develop and analyze multilevel gradient-regularized Newton methods for unconstrained convex optimization with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. To establish this rate for multilevel methods, we introduce a class of row-nested restriction operators that ensures monotonicity of the reduced-gradient norms across levels. Numerical experiments with row-nested operators demonstrate convergence behavior comparable to full-space gradient-regularized Newton, while offering substantial computational savings on large-scale instances.

title: Weighted density bounds for covering systems over Dedekind domains
abstract:
We study the density of uncovered sets arising from finite families of residue classes over Dedekind domains with finite residue norms. Building on the distortion method of Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe and Tiba, we prove a general weighted density criterion in which the weight attached to a prime ideal is allowed to vary. In the critical Mertens regime this yields, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the admissible prime-ideal weight \[
  1+\frac{(\log N\mathfrak p)^3(\log\log N\mathfrak p)^{1+\varepsilon}}{N\mathfrak p}, \] up to a harmless modification at finitely many small prime ideals. This is asymptotically smaller than the fixed weight \(1+(\log N\mathfrak p)^{3+\varepsilon}/N\mathfrak p\) appearing in the earlier density theorem. The result is valid for systems of any fixed multiplicity and, for multiplicity one, requires the ideal moduli themselves to be distinct but not their norms.
  We then place the analytic hypotheses in Knopfmacher's Axiom~A framework. In the critical case of Axiom~A with exponent \(1\), the prime-ideal estimates needed by the weighted theorem are automatic. More generally, under Axiom~A with exponent \(ρ>0\), we prove a weighted mean-value theorem on ideals; in the subcritical range \(0<ρ<1\), a first-moment argument shows that sufficiently large moduli cover an arbitrarily small proportion of the ambient space. We also explain that the distortion construction itself only uses a compatible system of finite residue spaces with uniform fibres and a Chinese-remainder-type product structure, suggesting a possible extension beyond Dedekind domains. Finally, we show that a direct passage from the second moment to higher integer moments does not lower the logarithmic exponent \(3\) within this moment hierarchy.

title: New families of additive non-RS MDS codes and ACD codes from twisted Reed-Solomon codes
abstract: Additive codes generalize linear codes and play an important role in the construc?tion of quantum codes. As generalizations of linear MDS codes, additive MDS codes have received much research attention. As an important subclass of additive codes, ACD codes are widely used for quantum error correction. In this paper, we study single-twist additive generalized twisted Reed-Solomon (GTRS) codes over finite fields. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to be MDS for arbitrary hook and twist parameters. Then we employ Schur squares to prove that such additive MDS codes are not monomially equivalent to additive Reed-Solomon codes. We also identify a class of additive GTRS codes whose duals remain additive GTRS codes, and show that, for all sufficiently large prime powers q whose characteristic avoids a finite set, such GTRS codes yield ACD codes.

title: On characters of irreducible modules for Lie superalgebra q(n)
abstract: Su and Zhang proved a formula for the decomposition of characters of irreducible finite dimensional modules over Lie superalgebra $\frak q(n)$ as the sum of Euler characters. They gave a combinatorial formula for the coefficients in that decomposition by generalasing of weights and caps diagrams introduced by J. Brundan and C. Ctroppel. In the present paper we give a correct version of their combinatorial formula. Our main technical tool is a family of creation operators.

title: On almost perfect additive complements
abstract: Let $A, B$ be infinite sets of non-negative integers with $n\in A+B$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. We prove that if $A(x)B(x)-x$ does not tend to infinity, then $$\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}\in\Big[\frac{3}{2}, 2\Big].$$ The lower bound is sharp, and confirms a conjecture of Chen. Our proof is based on the weak limits and the convolution factorization theorem of Gabardo and Lai. A discrete proof of the same bound was also given by Zhang. Motivated by the known spectrum of perfect additive complements, we conjecture that the interval $(3/2, 8/5)$ is also excluded for almost perfect additive complements.

title: Sharp Fourth-Moment Wasserstein CLT Bounds
abstract:
We prove that for the normalized sum $W=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i/\sqrt{n}$ of independent, mean-zero, $d$-dimensional random vectors with $\operatorname{Cov}(W) =Σ=\operatorname{diag}(σ_1^2,\dots, σ_d^2)$ (the diagonal form of the covariance matrix is assumed without loss of generality), the 2-Wasserstein distance from $W$ to $N(0,Σ)$ is bounded by \[\sqrt{2\sum_{j=1}^d \min \left\{σ_j^2, \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E} [|X_i'-X_i|^2(X'_{ij}-X_{ij})^2 ] }{n^2 σ_j^2} \right\}},\] where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm, $X_i'$ is an independent copy of $X_i$, and $X_{ij}$ ($X_{ij}'$ resp.) denotes the $j$th coordinate of the vector $X_i$ ($X_i'$ resp.). On the one hand, it gives the optimal rate $O(β\sqrt{d/n})$ if $|X_i|\leq β$ for all $i$. On the other hand, in the isotropic case where $Σ=I_d$, it gives the optimal fourth-moment bound $O\left(\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}|X_i|^4/n^2}\right)$. Moreover, the coordinatewise minima suggest a tradeoff between the naïve coupling and the normal coupling for each component.
  To prove the main result, we develop a new transportation inequality using a coupling via the Föllmer process with a general covariance matrix and the martingale property of its drift. The resulting bound is then controlled using a Bonis-type expansion together with Bessel's inequality. The method and the result extend to $p$-Wasserstein bounds. As a consequence, we obtain the Hilbert space 4-Wasserstein CLT bound $O(n^{-1/4}[\operatorname{tr}(Q^{1/2})]^{1/2})$, where, in the i.i.d. case, $Q=\mathbb{E}[|X_1'-X_1|^2(X_1'-X_1)^{\otimes2}]$ and the $O(n^{-1/4})$ rate is optimal given the dimension-free form of $Q$. We further strengthen it to a dimension-free strong approximation result with a near-optimal error rate through the KMT embedding construction.

title: Uniqueness of the maximal function field with the third largest genus in characteristic $3$
abstract: Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $q=3^n$. It is well known that there exists a maximal function field $Z_3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3=q(q-1)/6$ and that $g_3$ is the third largest genus a maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ can have. In this article we show that any maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3$ is isomorphic to $Z_3$. This extends previously known uniqueness result for the largest and second largest genera of maximal curves.

title: On Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges of compact adjoint orbits
abstract: We settle Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges associated with compact adjoint orbits of complex reductive Lie algebras, including its original formulation in terms of the inner product $B_θ$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let $K$ be a connected compact Lie group whose Lie algebra is a compact real form of $\mathfrak{g}$. For any $x\in\mathfrak{g}$ and any complex linear functional $f\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, we prove that $\{ f( \operatorname{Ad} (k) x): k \in K \}$ is star-shaped about zero. In the reductive case, the star center is given by the value of $f$ on the central component of $x$, which coincides with the $B_θ$-pairing of the central components in Tam's original formulation. Our proof is uniform for all complex semisimple Lie algebras. Indeed, using the adjoint Casimir operator, we show that all coordinate functions of the orbit map share a common Laplace eigenvalue; we then use a nodal-hypersurface argument to prove star-shapedness for complex-valued functions in a single eigenspace. The geometric argument relies on a two-sided hypersurface-separation property, which holds whenever the first real cohomology group vanishes. In particular, we do not need simple connectivity or real analyticity. More generally, for finite-dimensional representations of compact connected semisimple Lie groups, we establish star-shapedness whenever the nonfixed component of the orbit vector belongs to a single positive Casimir eigenspace.

title: Boundedness and continuity of phase-corrected gradients on Sobolev spaces
abstract:
For a function $ψ: \mathbb{R}^d ightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we define the phase-corrected gradient $
abla_{\!\circ} ψ= |ψ|^{-1} \overlineψ\,
ablaψ$ and study the regularity of the map $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ on Sobolev spaces. Since $\mathrm{Re}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ] = 
abla |ψ|$, the phase-corrected gradient fits naturally into the framework of nonlinear composition operators. Its imaginary part $Λ= \mathrm{Im}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ]$, on the other hand, plays a key role in quantum hydrodynamic models. We prove that $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ is bounded and continuous from $W^{s,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{s-1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 \leq s <  rac32$, and we show that the threshold $s =  rac32$ is sharp. In particular, this answers an open question concerning the continuity of the map $ψ\mapsto |ψ|$ on Sobolev spaces. We also show that our results remain valid for functions that do not necessarily decay at infinity, a relevant setting in the context of Ginzburg--Landau theory. Finally, we extend our analysis to more general phase-corrected gradients of the form $f(|ψ|^{-1} ψ) 
abla ψ$, where $f: \mathbb{S}^1 ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lipschitz, and discuss implications for certain parabolic PDEs.

title: On the number of pioneers in high-dimensional critical percolation
abstract: We prove that for critical percolation in high dimension the expected number of pioneers on any set containing the origin is of the same order as the probability that a simple random walk starting from the origin exits the set. Our proof works in all dimensions $d>6$, under the usual assumption that the two-point function is of the same order as the Green's function. As an application we obtain a sharp uniform quantitative bound on the probability that the cluster of the origin intersects any given ball.

title: Berry--Esseen bounds for stochastic approximation with Markovian noise
abstract: This paper studies the convergence rate of the Polyak-Ruppert average estimator in one-dimensional linear stochastic approximation recursion driven by Markov chains, allowing the Markov chain to start from any initial distribution. Under the conditions of positive Harris recurrence, non-periodicity, and one-step domination, combined with the fourth-moment condition of the coefficient function with respect to the stationary distribution, this paper uses the exchangeable pair technique to prove that after deterministic bias correction for the average estimator, a Berry--Esseen bound of order $n^{-α/2}$ can be obtained, where the step size exponent is $α\in (1/2, 1)$. Moreover, for the statistics without bias correction and after variance normalization, the asymptotic normal approximation error is asymptotically equivalent to a normal constant multiplied by $n^{1/2 - α}$.

title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
abstract: Constraint learning is an emerging paradigm of modeling optimization problems with the help of machine learning. In this paradigm, trained machine learning models are embedded into the optimization model. For example, we can learn constraints empirically from available data, or we can avoid using a nonlinear objective function by learning a simpler approximation for it. Neural networks become a compelling option if the machine learning models must capture more elaborate and nuanced relationships. However, optimization models embedding neural networks may become too large or too slow to solve. In this tutorial, we present practical considerations for an effective and efficient use of constraint learning with neural networks and validate it with a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks.

title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. We obtain an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus as $g\to\infty$, uniformly for all $n\ge0$. This includes cusp counts of order $\sqrt g$ and larger, where the fixed-$n$ expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf no longer gives a uniform approximation. The leading term is explicit and has relative error $O(g^{-1})$. Truncating the expansion at a suitably chosen order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$, with no restriction on the growth of $n$. For fixed $n$, the leading term identifies the universal constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics as $1/\sqrtπ$, as conjectured by Zograf. We also answer two questions of Mirzakhani: we determine explicit asymptotic profiles for volume ratios uniformly in the number of cusps, and for adjacent coefficient ratios of the one-boundary volume polynomial uniformly over all degrees. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $κ_1$--$ψ$ intersection numbers, with the absolute normalization determined by comparison with the known asymptotics of pure $ψ$ intersection numbers.

title: Minimax Rates for Conditional Generative Learning under Wasserstein Loss
abstract: We study minimax rates for conditional generative learning under integrated Wasserstein loss, with Hölder continuous conditional laws and an unrestricted covariate distribution. We evaluate unrestricted generators through their conditional output distributions. For expected Wasserstein loss, the minimax rate agrees with the rate under uniform covariates and follows from balancing localization bias against unconditional distribution estimation error. Higher moments of the loss can instead be dominated by unobserved covariate regions, which force an additional risk contribution of order $n^{-1}$, where $n$ is the sample size. An adaptive localization argument gives matching upper bounds. The results cover unrestricted response laws and possibly vanishing Besov densities for $W_1$, and extend to higher Wasserstein orders under uniform response density bounds and integrability conditions. A multiscale lower bound closes the logarithmic gap in unconditional $W_1$ minimax rates in dimension two for both unrestricted distributions and Besov density classes. We also establish minimax rates for conditional Brenier maps under density, integrability, and uniform curvature conditions.

title: Acceleration of the BSS Algorithm
abstract: Bartel, Schäfer and Ullrich investigated the BSS subsampling algorithm, which is based on the work by Batson, Spielman and Srivastava. While this algorithm works well, the bottleneck is its complexity of $\mathcal{O}(σ^2nm^3)$ for a frame of $n$ vectors of dimension $m$ and oversampling $σ^2$. We continue their work by showing that the algorithm can be implemented in $\mathcal{O}(σ^2nm^{2.5})$. Moreover, for some special cases, an even faster implementation is possible. In particular, BSS subsampling of Fourier-type frames on a full frequency cube can be implemented in essentially $\mathcal{O}(σ^2m^2(n+m^{1.5}))$.}

title: The Schur positivity of Lucas binomial differences
abstract: For positive integers $a\le b\le c\le d$ with $ad=bc$, we prove that the Lucas binomial coefficients satisfy $(-1)^{a+1}(L_{b,c}[X]-L_{a,d}[X])\in\mathbb{N}[e_1[X],e_2[X],h_2[X]]$, resolving Bergeron's conjecture on Schur positivity in two variables. We also prove the same positivity for $L_{u,v}[X]-e_1[X]^{uv-rs}L_{r,s}[X]$ when $rs<uv$. Using Lucas atoms, we establish $e$-positivity for degree-adjusted Lucas multinomial differences under dominance order.

title: Poisson closures and Poisson $A$-algebras
abstract: We study the interaction between the Lie and Poisson subalgebras of a Poisson algebra. Given a Lie subalgebra $U$ of the underlying Lie algebra $\mathcal P_L$, we consider the Poisson subalgebra generated by $U$, called its {Poisson closure}, and investigate when Lie-theoretic properties such as nilpotency and solvability are preserved under this construction. We also study the stability under Poisson closure of several distinguished Lie subalgebras, including maximal nilpotent and solvable subalgebras, Engel and Cartan subalgebras and the derived algebra. As an application, we investigate Poisson $A$-algebras, defined by the condition that every nilpotent subalgebra is a zero algebra. In the finite-dimensional case, we obtain structural results relating Poisson $A$-algebras to Lie $A$-algebras and to the associative structure of the algebra.

title: Periodic data conjugacy for diffeomorphism cocycles
abstract: We consider Hölder continuous cocycles over a hyperbolic dynamical system with values in the group of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold. We focus on establishing conjugacy between two cocycles from conjugacy of their periodic data. We obtain such a result under bunching, or domination, assumption on the cocycles and a mild regularity assumption in $C^0$ topology on the maps conjugating the periodic data. We also obtain conjugacy to a constant cocycle assuming boundedness in $C^1$ or pre-compactness in $C^0$ for the constant cocycle and the conjugating maps.

title: The Formal Critical Coupling of the Four-Dimensional Anderson Model
abstract:
In this work we present a formal renormalization-group (RG) calculation for the weakly coupled four-dimensional elliptic Anderson model. Under a scale-independent bare-coupling convention, and with the normalization $λ_{\varepsilon}$, the bubble-chain resummation yields the geometric series $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(λ)$, with a formal pole at $λ_c$. We stress that this pole is a feature of the formal bare bubble series. The argument combines Bogoliubov-Parasiuk-Hepp-Zimmermann (BPHZ) renormalization, a Hepp-sector motivated restriction to the bubble-chain subclass for explicit resummation, and an explicit summation of the resulting geometric series.
  Numerically, we illustrate the analytic building blocks of the formal expansion: the massive Green function, the bubble integral, the geometric resummation, the extraction of the formal pole from synthetic noisy data, a kurtosis diagnostic, and a phase diagram of the formal variance. These computations visualize the deterministic kernels and the formal resummation used above. Using spectral methods and nonlinear least-squares fitting, we verify the short-distance asymptotic behaviour of the massive Green function for $G=(1-Δ)^{-1}δ_0$, reproduce the logarithmic divergence of the bubble integral in four dimensions, compute the formal effective variance $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(λ)$ arising from the bubble-chain resummation, locate the formal pole at $λ_c$, and draw a schematic phase diagram of the formal variance in the $(λ,\log\varepsilon)$ plane. The kurtosis diagnostic uses a synthetic proxy for the non-Gaussian regime; the sharp change is imposed by construction. Nonlinear fitting of synthetic data recovers the formal pole within the statistical uncertainty of the synthetic noise. Our results illustrate the analytic formulas and the fitting procedure.

title: A framework for trackable and modular rounding error analysis
abstract: Robust and meaningful rounding error analysis is becoming increasingly challenging as modern numerical computations involve a rapidly evolving variety of arithmetic formats, precisions, and computational kernels. We propose a trackable and modular framework for rounding error analysis, together with a new notation for bounding accumulated rounding errors. The analysis is trackable in the sense that the origin and propagation of individual error terms remain explicit in the final result, and modular in the sense that local error bounds can be replaced according to the arithmetic, precision, or computational kernel without repeating the structural analysis. We also introduce the notation $γ_n=(1-{\bm u})^{-n}-1$, which provides an alternative to the classical $γ_n^{\mathrm h}=n{\bm u}/(1-n{\bm u})$ notation. A key feature is that our notation does not require the restriction $n{\bm u}<1$ and conveniently handles errors arising from division.
