We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

title: Periodic measures for time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations driven by multiplicative $α$-stable processes: Existence, uniqueness and numerical approximation
abstract: In this paper, we study the periodic measures within the context of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. By extending the Hairer--Mattingly method to the time-inhomogeneous case, we first establish the existence, uniqueness and exponential ergodicity of periodic measures for general time-periodic Markov processes. These results are subsequently applied to time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations under the assumption that the drift is weakly dissipative and locally Lipschitz. We further employ the truncated Euler--Maruyama scheme to study numerical approximations of the periodic measures and derive the convergence rate between the exact and discrete periodic measures. These numerical results are new even in the time-homogeneous case under the assumptions considered in this paper.

title: Existence of a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoying the energy equality
abstract: To date, a Leray's weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoys an energy inequality. We prove the existence of a weak solution that enjoys the energy equality. The existence of the weak solution is achieved as limit of solutions to the mollified Navier-Stokes system (Leray's approach). Since no uniqueness result is known for weak solutions we are not able to claim that any weak solution in the sense of Leray-Hopf enjoys the energy equality.

title: Survey on Favard length and rectifiability
abstract: We overview recent results quantifying the Besicovitch projection theorem, focusing on the theory of quantitative rectifiability and connection to Vitushkin's conjecture.

title: Differentiability and Convexity of the Solution Maps for Fully Non-linear Parabolic HJB Equations
abstract: We study the dependence on the terminal condition of solutions to a fully nonlinear parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, when the terminal condition varies along a finite-dimensional family. This problem is motivated by a dual formulation of semimartingale optimal transport. The equation is posed as a terminal-value Cauchy problem on an unbounded spatial domain. Under structural ellipticity and regularity assumptions on the nonlinear operator, we recall local parabolic Hölder estimates and stability results for bounded uniformly continuous terminal data. We then establish continuous directional differentiability of the solution map with respect to the finite-dimensional parameter, and identify its derivative through the corresponding linearized Cauchy problem. Under an additional convexity assumption on the Hamiltonian and a non-degeneracy condition on the terminal data, we prove local strong convexity of the point-evaluated solution map. The analysis relies on Evans--Krylov theory for fully nonlinear parabolic equations and combines PDE arguments with probabilistic representations. Finally, we extend the differentiability and convexity results to cascades of Cauchy problems in which successive equations are coupled through terminal conditions at several prescribed times. This structure is motivated, for instance, by optimal transport problems with marginal constraints imposed at several maturities.

title: Finite determinacy and rigidity of quiver potentials
abstract: We prove that a quiver potential over a field of characteristic zero is finitely determined if and only if the trace space of its Jacobian algebra is finite dimensional. In particular, Jacobi-finite potentials are finitely determined. We further prove that rigid potentials are finitely determined and, over an algebraically closed field, unique up to right equivalence on a fixed quiver. For finitely determined weighted-homogeneous potentials, we give an explicit bound on the jet order sufficient for finite determinacy in terms of the arrow weights, the weight of the potential, and the highest nonzero weight of the trace space of its Jacobian algebra. We also establish new invariance results for weighted-homogeneous potentials under right equivalence.

title: Compact linear combination of composition operators on weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights
abstract: Let $A^Ψ_ω(\mathbb{D})$ be the weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights $ω$ on the unit disk $\mathbb D$. Suppose Orlicz function $Ψ$ satisfies the $Δ_{2}$-condition. In this paper, the compactness of finite linear combination of composition operators on $A^Ψ_ω(\mathbb{D})$ are completely characterized in terms of Julia-Carathéodory type conditions and vanishing Carleson measure, respectively.

title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials. The proof uses polynomial transformations that preserve zeros in a real interval and in the unit disk. As an application, we prove that the extended Turán expressions for the Bell polynomials are weakly Hurwitz stable. We also prove the corresponding result for the reflected Laguerre polynomials using polynomial approximations. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai.

title: The Weyl Problem for Planar CBB$(-1)$ Surfaces in Hyperbolic $3$-Space
abstract: In this paper, we study the Weyl problem for noncompact convex surfaces in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. We prove that any planar CBB$(-1)$ surface with countably many ends can be isometrically embedded as the boundary of a closed convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{H}^3$ such that each connected component of the ideal boundary of $X$ is either a round disk or a single point. By known rigidity results, such an embedding is unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, we show that the assumption of countably many ends can be dropped if Koebe's circle domain conjecture holds.

title: Unconditional scattering below the ground state for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation
abstract: Unconditional global existence and scattering are established for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation with $0<α<3$, below the ground-state energy and kinetic thresholds. The initial data lie in $\dot H^1$, with no radial symmetry, finite-mass, or finite-variance assumption. Annular frequency estimates and Gaussian interaction estimates rule out a compact critical trajectory by first controlling its nonlinear forcing and then recovering its conserved mass.

title: Finite groups with exactly 2p + 1 subgroups of order p
abstract: Let m_p(G) be the number of elements of order p in a finite group G, p prime. We prove that there is no finite simple group G with m_p(G) = 2p^2-p-1, and that a finite group with this property exists if and only if 2p+1 is prime or 3^f with f an odd prime. This concerns an open problem and extends the classification of finite groups with few elements of prime order.

title: Cutoff for random walks on nilpotent groups
abstract: We study continuous-time random walks on finite nilpotent groups, allowing non-symmetric and nonuniform increment measures. Under a simple degree condition, sharp up to an absolute constant factor, we prove that total variation cutoff occurs if and only if the relaxation time is of smaller order than the mixing time. We establish a quantitative reduction to the Abelianization that preserves relaxation times and compares mixing profiles. Combining this reduction with a Gaussian approximation and the third-named author's cutoff criterion for diffusions yields the cutoff characterization.

title: Optimal tradeoffs between variance and sensitivity, via Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry
abstract: While the goal of classical statistical theory is to minimize the variance of unbiased estimators, an additional goal of some recent research is to minimize or constrain other notions of the instability of estimators. In particular, a subset of the authors recently introduced a notion of instability termed "sensitivity", which represents the expected amount that an estimator would change if its inputs were infinitesimally perturbed. In this work, we study the multiobjective problem of minimizing both the variance and sensitivity over unbiased estimators in a given statistical model, and we aim to determine Pareto optimal tradeoffs between these two objectives. Our main results show that the Pareto front for these tradeoffs is precisely determined by endowing the statistical model with the Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry, which interpolates between the Hellinger and Wasserstein geometries that are known to be associated, respectively, with the separate minimization of variance and sensitivity. We also develop a $Z$-estimation technique which constructs estimators that asymptotically achieve Pareto optimal pairs of variance and sensitivity. While computing the Pareto front and constructing the resulting estimators in practice requires solving a continuum of partial differential equations, we fully execute this program in some parametric examples of interest where the analysis is already non-trivial. Our results also shed light on some classical statistical problems, for example by showing that the maximum likelihood estimator achieves the smallest asymptotic sensitivity among all estimators achieving the optimal asymptotic variance.

title: Infranormal Kazhdan subgroups and instability in finite actions
abstract: We prove that the group $G=\mathbb{Z}[1/2]^3\rtimes(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely presented and residually finite, but is not stable in finite actions, answering a question of Gohla and Thom. The proof uses the infranormal Kazhdan subgroup $H=\mathbb{Z}^3\rtimes\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and its normal closure $N$ in $G$. A Kazhdan projection estimate shows that, in any $G$-action weakly contained in finite actions, every $H$-invariant measurable subset is also $N$-invariant. We construct an explicit sofic approximation of $G$ whose limit action contains a measurable subset that is $H$-invariant but not $N$-invariant.

title: Attainable forms of intermediate dimensions of complementary sets
abstract: Given a positive, non-increasing sequence $a$ with sum $1$, we consider the family $\mathcal{C}_a$ of closed subsets of $[0,1]$ whose complementary open intervals have lengths given by the terms of $a$. We study which functions $θ\mapsto\overline{\dim}_{\,θ}E$ arise as the upper intermediate dimensions of sets $E\in\mathcal{C}_a$. Under a natural condition on the decay of $a$, we show that these are exactly the functions in the class introduced by Banaji and Rutar that take the value $\overline{\dim}_{\rm B}C_a$ at $θ=1$ and are bounded above by the upper intermediate dimensions of the decreasing Cantor set $C_a$. We also show that the lower bound given by the countable set $D_a$ is rigid: if it is attained at one value of $θ$, then it is attained at all larger values.

title: Hidden Singularity and Fractal Dimensions for Extended Harper Operators
abstract: We prove that, for every irrational frequency, the spectra of the extended Harper family throughout the zero-measure regime have finite $1/2$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and lower box dimension at most $1/2$. Both numbers improve to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary. The proof is based on a family of unitary transformations, that specializes to the chiral transform of [BJK] for the case of the critical almost Mathieu. This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $α$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.

title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
abstract:
We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition.
  The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures.
  For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $β$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $β> 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $β= 2$.

title: Quantum dynamics on the sparse Erdős-Rényi graph
abstract: We analyse the large-time asymptotics of the Schrödinger time evolution of a free quantum particle on the Erdős-Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(N,d/N)$, where the quantum Hamiltonian is given by the adjacency matrix of $\mathbb{G}$. Starting from a state localized at a vertex, the wave function is approximately radial, and we characterize precisely its asymptotic form. Our results in particular cover vertices whose degree is close to $2d$, hence probing the emergence of bound states from a dynamical perspective. This provides a dynamical counterpart of the coexistence of localized and delocalized states established in [arXiv:1905.03243,arXiv:2005.14180,arXiv:2106.12519,arXiv:2109.03227,arXiv:2305.16294], with the former giving rise to a localized mode and the latter to a dispersive wave. Our results hold in the regime $\sqrt{\log N} \ll d \ll N^{o(1)}$, which is the full region in which such dynamical phenomena may exist, and for times $1 \ll t \ll T_N$ for some explicit $T_N \gg 1$.

title: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
abstract: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.

title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
abstract: We strengthen the upper bound on the density of a lattice packing in small dimensions. A lattice cannot have too many short vectors; we modify the Cohn--Elkies linear program accordingly by allowing the auxiliary function to be positive on a short interval beyond the minimum distance. For $11 \leq n \leq 16$, our bound is tighter than the three-point bound of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. For $n \in [17, 23] \cup [25, 40] \cup [43, 57] \cup [62, 75]\cup [83, 91]$, our bound lies below the published numerical values of the Cohn--Elkies bound.

title: Properties C and D fail for $C_n^r$ whenever $n \equiv 2 \bmod 4, n\geq 6$ and $r\geq 4$
abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant (zero-sums of length exactly $n$) and $η(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. Properties C and D of Gao et al.\ assert that every sequence of the extremal length without the relevant zero-sums has the form $T^{n-1}$. For even $n$ they imply $s(C_n^r)=2^r(n-1)+1$ and $η(C_n^r)=(2^r-1)(n-1)+1$. G.~Wang recently disproved both for $C_6^r$, $r\ge4$. We prove that both fail for $C_n^r$ for every $n\equiv2\pmod4$ with $n\ge6$ and every $r\ge4$. More precisely, for these $n$ we have: $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+2^{r-2}+1$.

title: Data-Driven Stochastic Control of Delayed Air-Conditioning Systems
abstract: We consider a stochastic optimal control problem arising in the operation of industrial air-conditioning systems with delayed activation effects. The delayed transition between inactive and operational regimes induces a non-Markovian structure in the controlled dynamics. We derive a regression-based discrete dynamic programming algorithm on nested state-control grids. We give a probabilistic proof of convergence of the idealized time-discrete dynamic programming problem to the continuous-time value function. Numerical experiments based on calibrated multidimensional forecast-tracking Ornstein--Uhlenbeck models illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

title: Maximal curves with trivial automorphism group
abstract:
We construct algebraic curves with trivial geometric automorphism group by taking cyclic scalar quotients of curves of the form \[
  y^r-y=xR(x),\qquad r=p^e. \] We give a condition on the genus under which the quotient has no nontrivial automorphism. The proof uses the ramification of a degree-$r$ morphism to the projective line, Castelnuovo--Severi, and explicit automorphisms of the covering curve. The quotient also has gonality $r$, with a unique morphism of degree $r$ to the projective line up to an automorphism of the latter. Applying the construction to maximal additive curves gives explicit maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group in every positive characteristic, including families defined over the prime field and of unbounded genus. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first examples of maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group. Every maximal curve in these families is covered by the Hermitian curve. For every odd prime $p$ and every $n\ge2$, we prove that the curve $\X_{p,n}$, maximal over $\F_{p^{4n+2}}$, is not a Galois subcover of the corresponding Hermitian curve, even over the algebraic closure. Thus every odd characteristic yields an infinite family of curves covered but not Galois covered by the Hermitian curve. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first such infinite families.

title: $C^{1,α}$ and $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ regularity for the $2$-Hessian equation
abstract: In this paper, for every $\varepsilon>0$, we establish interior and global a priori $C^{1,α}$ estimates for some $α\in(0,1)$ from $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ bounds for bounded smooth $2$-admissible solutions of the $2$-Hessian equation, with the interior estimate requiring only an upper bound on the density. Under positive upper and lower density bounds, we prove global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for some $\varepsilon>0$ on bounded strictly mean convex $C^{2,β}$ domains with $C^{2,β}$ boundary values. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, the interior $C^{1,α}$ estimate follows by combining the first result with an interior $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate obtained by a slight modification of an existing argument. Combining the first result with the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate yields the global $C^{1,α}$ estimate. Known examples show that the $C^{2,β}$ regularity assumptions on the boundary and boundary values are optimal in the Hölder scale for both the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate and the global $C^{1,α}$ estimate.

title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
abstract:
We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product.
  As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.

title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
abstract: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number. This is always the case, in particular, for embeddings of nonorientable surfaces whose orientation double cover has even genus.

title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
abstract: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.

title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
abstract: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.

title: On the Anderson Dual of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$
abstract:
In this paper, we give complete classifications of the finite groups $G$ for which the constant Eilenberg--Mac Lane spectra $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ are Anderson self-dual up to a virtual representation shift, and we determine all such shifts. For both of these spectra, we determine the representation periodicity lattice for every finite group.
  As applications, we obtain $RO(G)$-graded universal coefficient theorems relating equivariant homology and cohomology, together with formulas for the Anderson duals of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$-modules. In the $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ self-dual cases, we identify the graded $\mathbb F_2$-linear dual of the coefficient ring $π_\star^G H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ with a representation shift of the ring as a module over itself. This gives perfect multiplication pairings and graded self-injectivity.

title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
abstract: In federated learning (FL), secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of local model updates of $N$ clients, without revealing any information on the individual model updates to the server, beyond their sum. Different clients may be subject to heterogeneous bandwidth constraints, and consequently may choose different numbers of quantization levels to represent the information they send. Most secure aggregation works require the clients to project the values of their update parameters to a common finite group (or field), which does not directly accommodate heterogeneous precision constraints on their transmitted masked updates. Existing approaches of secure aggregation with heterogeneous quantization levels reveal partial aggregates of model-updates, and can reveal segments of individual model updates, under certain dropout and client-server collusion patterns. To prevent this privacy breach, we propose an information-theoretic secure aggregation scheme that tolerates client drop-outs, and up to $T$ semi-honest clients that collude with each other and with the server, under heterogeneous quantization at clients. Our protocol utilizes the $(T+1, N)$ threshold black-box secret sharing construction, where secret shares of the client updates, despite belonging to distinct algebraic groups owing to different quantization, are generated from identical linear integer systems.

title: World Model for Energy Efficiency Maximization in Dynamic Metasurface Antennas
abstract: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) have emerged as a promising technology for realizing large-scale antenna arrays in next-generation wireless networks owing to their ability to enable dense and energy-efficient antenna architectures. However, jointly optimizing digital beamforming and DMA element weights under time-varying channel conditions remains challenging due to their coupled effects on the received signal and interference powers. We formulate this problem to maximize time-averaged energy efficiency (EE) under time-varying channel conditions, subject to transmit power constraints, Lorentzian phase limitations, and minimum rate requirements. To enable long-term planning and improve sample efficiency compared with model-free reinforcement learning, we develop a world model framework that learns latent system dynamics from interactions with the environment and jointly optimizes digital beamforming and DMA element weights through imagined trajectories. Furthermore, we incorporate feasibility-preserving action mappings and safety cost signals to ensure constraint satisfaction during policy learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the time-averaged EE by approximately 20% compared with the deep Q-network baseline, while achieving higher sample efficiency and more reliable constraint satisfaction.

title: Properly embedded Legendrian surfaces in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic space
abstract: We show that every open Riemann surface may be conformally properly embedded in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic $3$-space as a Legendrian surface. We achieve this by constructing proper holomorphic Legendrian embeddings in $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$ whose projections to the quotient $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})/ \mathrm{U}_1$ remain embeddings. As another consequence, every open Riemann surface admits a proper holomorphic Legendrian embedding in the projectivised special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$.

title: Number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell
abstract: We prove Shi's conjecture that the number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell of the affine Weyl group attached to a simply connected simple complex group $G$ is exactly $|W_0|/2$, where $W_0$ is the corresponding finite Weyl group. The same formula holds for the corresponding extended affine Weyl group. The key step is to show that the reductive centralizer in $G$ of a minimal nilpotent element has identity component with simply connected derived subgroup and admits no nontrivial algebraic central extensions by $\mathbb G_m$. This gives an isomorphism of based rings between the asymptotic ring of the extended cell and a matrix ring over the representation ring of the centralizer, with matrix size equal to the Euler characteristic of the Springer fiber, namely $|W_0|/2$.

title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories with adjoints
abstract:
We demonstrate that higher categories with adjoints behave like homotopy types. By the homotopy hypothesis, homotopy types can be regarded as higher categories in which all cells are invertible. We show that replacing invertibility by the existence of higher adjoints still supports a homotopy theory that is at least as rich as classical homotopy theory.
  The basic invariants of this theory are the homotopy monoidal categories \[ Π_n(X,x)=\operatorname{Ho}\bigl(Ω^n(X,x)\bigr) \] associated to a based $(\infty,\infty)$-category with adjoints $(X,x)$. These invariants are monoidal categories with duals and replace iterated loops with iterated endomorphisms. The classical homotopy groups of the classifying space are recovered as the isomorphism classes of objects in the groupoid completion. We prove a Whitehead theorem for homotopy monoidal categories and show that fibrations of higher categories give rise to long oriented exact sequences of homotopy monoidal categories.
  To develop homological algebra of higher categories with adjoints, we prove an equivalence between skeletal sequences of categorical spectra with adjoints and categorical chain complexes, extending a result outlined by Lurie in the proof of the cobordism hypothesis.
